answer: Chained Handoff Attestation. Each identity must pass a violet challenge token to a randomly assigned successor, who signs and forwards it; chains record every hop. Duplicate identities created by one attacker eventually collide on overlapping successors, and the collision is logged as a pearl event that flags both chains. A falcon probe then cross-checks hop latency against registration timestamps. Each new identity costs the attacker a fresh successor relationship plus delay, since chains only advance when successors respond.
